item.title: Text-to-Image Models and Their Representation of People from Different Nationalities Engaging in Activities
item.headline: A high image score can miss an awkward stereotype
item.summary: Image scorers often rewarded nationality-linked clothing even when unsuitable for the activity. This manuscript tests specific models and prompts, not current products generally.

evidence.question: Does matching a prompt ensure an appropriate depiction?
evidence.method: Manually labeled 2,060 DALL-E 3/Gemini 3 Pro Preview images: 206 nationalities, five activities; compared scores across caption variants.
evidence.limitations: One image per combination; subjective clothing labels; generations collected at different times in 2025.

explainer.finding: Across both generators, 15.9% of soccer/jogging images had clothing labeled impractical.
explainer.method: CLIP, an open-source ALIGN implementation, and GPT-4.1 mini evaluated image–caption matches.
explainer.meaning: A soccer scene can score well for matching a nationality cue while dressing players unsuitably: relevance and appropriateness need separate checks.
explainer.limits: Traditional clothing is not inherently inappropriate. Scores do not measure community preferences; this comparison does not isolate causes.
